topics.name: Living and non-living things
subtopics: There are many different kinds of living things
Living plants and animals carry out all seven life processes: feeding, growing, reproducing, breathing, excreting, sensing, moving
Some things appear not to be living (dried beans, dried yeast, fertilised egg) but carry on living given the right conditions
Non-living things cannot carry out all seven life processes; some things were living and are now dead
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Structure of plants and animals
subtopics: Basic structure of plants: roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, seeds
Visible differences between plants in size, shape and colour of their parts
Basic structure of animals: head, tail, body, limbs, sense organs
Visible differences between animals in size, shape, body covering and sense organs
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: What plants need to grow
subtopics: Plants need light, water and air to grow
New plants can grow from cuttings and seeds
Seeds need water and warmth to germinate
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Habitats of animals
subtopics: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives; grassland, forest, river and sea habitats
Animals need a habitat for food, water, shelter, having babies and escaping danger
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Structures for animal shelters
subtopics: Natural animal shelters (nests, shells, hollow trees, wasp nests) and human-made shelters (kennels, cages, kraals, stables)
Animal shelters can be shell or frame structures of different shapes, sizes and materials
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Materials around us
subtopics: Solids, liquids and gases make up all materials; properties of each (solids keep shape, liquids flow, gases spread out)
Heating and cooling cause changes of state: melting, evaporating, condensing, freezing/solidifying
Water evaporates, condenses, freezes and melts in the water cycle

topics.name: Solid materials
subtopics: Raw materials used to make other materials: sand to glass, clay to ceramics, coal and oil to plastics, wood to paper, wool and hide to fabrics and leather
Properties of raw and manufactured materials: hard/soft, stiff/flexible, strong/weak, light/heavy, waterproof/absorbent

topics.name: Strengthening materials
subtopics: Ways to strengthen materials such as paper to build a strong structure
Fold paper into hollow circular, triangular or square pillars; roll paper into tubes (struts)

topics.name: Strong frame structures
subtopics: Struts joined into triangular shapes make strong, stable frame structures (roof trusses, bridges, cranes, pylons, skeletons)
Indigenous homes (Zulu uguqa, Xhosa rontabile and ungqu-phantsi, Nama matjieshuis) use a framework of struts

topics.name: Energy and energy transfer
subtopics: We use energy for everything we do and get our energy from food
Energy in food comes from the Sun: plants use sunlight to make food
Energy is transferred from the Sun to plants to animals in an energy chain/food chain

topics.name: Energy around us
subtopics: Energy around us includes movement, heat, light and sound; energy is stored in food, wood, coal, oil products and natural gas
Energy can be transferred from a source to where it is needed
Machines and appliances need input energy and provide useful output energy

topics.name: Movement and energy in a system
subtopics: Musical instruments (systems) use movement input energy such as blowing, beating and plucking
Instruments have parts that move or vibrate and produce sound as the main output energy

topics.name: Energy and sound
subtopics: Musical instruments make sounds through vibrations; vibrations travel outwards through air, water, plastic, metal and wood
Sounds can be loud or soft (volume) and high or low (pitch)
Noise pollution can cause permanent hearing damage

topics.name: Planet Earth
subtopics: The Earth is a sphere made of rock; main surface features are land, water and air
Most of the Earth's surface is covered by oceans and seas; land is made up of continents and islands; a thin layer of air surrounds the Earth
The Earth has many different habitats
The Earth is a planet in space; from Earth we see the Sun, Moon and stars

topics.name: The Sun
subtopics: The Sun is a star made of hot gas that gives out heat and light
The Sun is much bigger than the Earth, very far away, but the closest star to Earth
The Sun provides heat and light for living things

topics.name: The Earth and Sun
subtopics: The Earth moves around the Sun in an orbit; the Sun is at the centre of the solar system
The Earth is one of eight planets in the solar system
The Earth gets the right amount of light and heat from the Sun to support life

topics.name: The Moon
subtopics: The Moon is a ball of rock with no air or water, smaller than the Earth and closer to Earth than the Sun
Phases of the Moon: the changing pattern of sunlight on the Moon repeats every 29½ days
Cultural stories about the Moon

topics.name: Rocket systems
subtopics: People have used rockets to go into space and travel to the Moon
A rocket is a system that propels vehicles into space by pushing exhaust gases out of its back end
